title: 2008 AMC 12A Problem 3
statement: Suppose that \(\tfrac{2}{3}\) of \(10\) bananas are worth as much as \(8\) oranges. How many oranges are worth as much as \(\tfrac{1}{2}\) of \(5\) bananas?

solutions.text:
Since \(\tfrac{2}{3}\) of \(10\) bananas is \(\tfrac{20}{3}\) bananas, worth \(8\) oranges, one banana is worth \[ 8 \div \dfrac{20}{3} = \dfrac{24}{20} = \dfrac{6}{5} \] oranges.

Then \(\tfrac{1}{2}\) of \(5\) bananas is \(\tfrac{5}{2}\) bananas, worth \[ \dfrac{5}{2} \cdot \dfrac{6}{5} = 3 \] oranges.

Thus, C is the correct answer.
